# The Origin Engine API

`@origingame/engine`, API version 1: 42 modules, generated from `crates/og-api/api.ogt`. Each module has an overview page and every function, component and type a page of its own under `<module>/`; every signature is quoted from the IDL. `og api find <words>` ranks every entry; `og api show <name>` prints one.

The Origin Engine API. Game code declares components and systems, and reads the world through typed views over engine memory.

Every failure is a returned Result; desc objects may omit any field; nothing reads the wall clock inside a tick.

## Modules

| Module | TypeScript | Publish builds | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`math`](math.md) | types and tokens | kept | Plain math values in the three.js vocabulary. They are data: the engine owns the operations, so results are identical on every host. |
| [`reflect`](reflect.md) | named exports | kept | Reflection: components and resources are declared once with their field layout and metadata, and registered by name. |
| [`world`](world.md) | types and tokens | kept | The world: an archetype ECS. Entities are generational handles; components are columns in engine memory. |
| [`system`](system.md) | named exports | kept | Systems: functions the engine calls once per tick with their matched archetypes. |
| [`game`](game.md) | `og.*` | kept | The game entry: what the bundle's default export declares. |
| [`transform`](transform.md) | `og.transform.*` | kept | Transforms in the three.js vocabulary: position, quaternion and scale, composed into matrixWorld down the parent chain. |
| [`time`](time.md) | `og.time.*` | kept | Simulation time. Game code never reads the wall clock; it reads Time. |
| [`rng`](rng.md) | types and tokens | kept | Deterministic randomness. Every random draw comes from an Rng stream; the sequence for a seed is identical on every host and in the Web scaffold's rng.ts. |
| [`procgen`](procgen.md) | `og.procgen.*` | kept | Procedural generation: gradient noise (Perlin, simplex, FBM), Poisson-disk points, BSP dungeons and wave function collapse, all deterministic. Each generator takes a `seed` (a fork of og.Rng's, so the main stream does not move) and draws only from a stream on it, in a fixed order, with bit-identical arithmetic: the same seed gives the same output on every host, in a replay and after a restore. |
| [`input`](input.md) | `og.input.*` | kept | Input as the game sees it: the Input resource for polling, events for edges, og.Pointers for several pointers at once (multi-touch) and og.Gamepad for up to eight pads. All of it is world state, so it replays. |
| [`camera`](camera.md) | `og.camera.*` | kept | The main camera, as a resource with three.js PerspectiveCamera and OrthographicCamera parameter names. |
| [`render`](render.md) | `og.render.*` | kept | What is drawn: meshes with materials. Draws are instanced by (geometry, material) automatically; there is no per-object draw call. |
| [`shapes`](shapes.md) | types and tokens | kept | Two-dimensional outlines in three.js's words: og.Shape and og.Path2 are three.js's Shape and Path, built by the same calls (moveTo, lineTo, bezierCurveTo, arc, absarc, ellipse, closePath, ...) and flattened to points by getPoints. og.render.shapeGeometry, extrudeGeometry and sweepGeometry take them; only their points cross to the engine. |
| [`load`](load.md) | `og.load.*` | kept | Asset loading from cooked output: `og cook` turns assets/ into cooked/ (.ogb blobs and the manifest cooked/.cook.ogt), and the runtime reads only cooked/. |
| [`physics`](physics.md) | `og.physics.*` | kept | Rigid bodies over rapier (rapier3d in the 3D profile, rapier2d in 2D, both with enhanced determinism): game code owns the components, the engine's og.physics system steps them after the game's systems and writes the dynamic bodies back. |
| [`atmosphere`](atmosphere.md) | `og.atmosphere.*` | kept | Fog, a procedural sky, the day-night cycle, weather, the wind that sways vegetation and water, declared as resources and components (the E5 round). Everything is off by default: a world that sets none of them draws exactly as before. |
| [`anim`](anim.md) | `og.anim.*` | kept | Skeletal animation over og-anim: glTF skins and clips (loaded with og.load.animation), blend-tree graphs with layered state machines, root motion, two-bone and FABRIK IK and blendshapes, evaluated by the engine's og.anim system after the game's systems and before physics. |
| [`tween`](tween.md) | `og.tween.*` | kept | Tweens: animate any numeric field of a component (og.Transform.position, a game's own f32) to a target over time with an easing curve, a delay, repeat and yoyo, in sequences or in parallel. Advanced by og.tween after the game's systems, before og.anim and physics, by scaled time unless unscaled. |
| [`tilemap`](tilemap.md) | `og.tilemap.*` | kept | Tilemaps: layers of tiles from a tileset atlas (a `type tileset` `.ogt`), loaded from a cooked map (a `type tilemap` `.ogt`, a Tiled `.tmj` or an LDtk `.ldtk`) with og.load.tilemap and placed by an og.Tilemap component; og.tilemap.create and og.tilemap.resize make and change maps in game code. |
| [`audio`](audio.md) | `og.audio.*` | kept | Sound: inside the tick, the engine's og.audio system (after the game's systems and physics) turns AudioSource changes into a deterministic, time-stamped command stream; outside the tick the host's mixer renders it (an AudioWorklet on the web, the output device, a capture or a null sink natively). |
| [`nav`](nav.md) | `og.nav.*` | kept | Navigation: grids (A* and jump point search, eight-way moves that never cut a blocked corner, line-of-sight smoothing), flow fields for crowds, and navmeshes (cooked, or built at runtime) with funnel paths and box obstacles that rebuild only the tiles they touch. |
| [`ai`](ai.md) | `og.ai.*` | kept | Enemy and NPC AI as data: behaviour trees (BehaviorTree.CPP's control names) and tick state machines in `.ogt` files of `type behaviour`, perception (sight cones checked against physics occlusion, hearing of spatial sounds and game noises) and a blackboard per agent. |
| [`story`](story.md) | `og.story.*` | kept | Dialogue and quests: Yarn Spinner 3.2.2 dialogue in `.yarn` files (declaring `#og-profile:yarn-spinner-3.2.2`), compiled by og cook, every line and option with an explicit stable `#line:` id; quests as `type quest` data with stages, reflected event objectives and rewards. |
| [`platform`](platform.md) | `og.platform.*` | kept | Platform services as host capabilities: the cloud store and save slots, leaderboards, telemetry, Origin Point, AI marks, purchases, ads, achievements, the player, friends, invites, share and rooms. Game code names a method and its arguments, never a credential, a URL or a cookie: the host owns them; every id it hands back is opaque and scoped to this game. Calls are asynchronous: each returns a request number at once and its answer arrives at the start of a later tick (og.PlatformAnswered, og.platform.result), host input like key presses. A host that lacks a method answers it `unavailable`. |
| [`i18n`](i18n.md) | `og.i18n.*` | kept | Localization: one string table per locale (`.ogt` of `type strings`), messages in a subset of ICU MessageFormat with CLDR plural rules, and the locale the host asks for. The active locale is the best loaded table for the request, else the base table; a key it lacks is read from its `fallback` table, then the base. It also sets the UI's font chain and direction. |
| [`ui`](ui.md) | `og.ui.*` | kept | The engine's UI: an immediate-mode toolkit. Systems describe the tree every tick with these calls; the engine lays it out Clay-style, styles it with the game's UI style (the engine's default style until the game picks one), draws it over the frame and answers the probe (dump_ui, touch_move_to, move_to_text) from it. |
| [`systems`](systems.md) | types and tokens | kept | Systems the engine ships as TypeScript: game-level code, listed explicitly in GameDesc.systems like the game's own, so the schedule (and dump_world) shows them and nothing runs that the game did not ask for. |
| [`commands`](commands.md) | `og.commands.*` | dropped | The command channel: actions scheduled on simulation time, from `og run --commands "t:action[:args];..."` or the probe's commands(). |
| [`probe`](probe.md) | types and tokens | kept | The probe: RuntimeProbe protocol 5 (origin/packages/contracts/src/probe.ts) served natively, plus the engine's wire members. |
| [`terrain`](terrain.md) | `og.terrain.*` | kept | Terrain (phase 2): a height field over a rectangle, cooked by `og cook` from a `type terrain` .ogt (a heightmap, a control map, up to sixteen layered materials, a holes map) into tiles; drawn as a clipmap around the camera, collided with as a height field, baked into navmeshes. |
| [`stream`](stream.md) | `og.stream.*` | kept | Asset streaming groups (phase 3): a scene's `stream "<name>" { asset ...; distance ... \| volume ...; priority n }` blocks name assets that load and unload together, one pack each, admitted by priority within a memory budget (256 MiB by default). Until resident, models draw proxies, textures a placeholder and sounds silence of their own length, so nothing a tick reads depends on what is resident. |
| [`video`](video.md) | `og.video.*` | kept | Footage in a game (docs/design.md §2.9): a `type video` asset cooked by ffmpeg, loaded with og.load.video and played by og.VideoPlayer. A clip (the default: at most 256 frames) is cooked into a texture array; a stream (`stream true`: any length) is cooked to AV1 and decoded as it plays. The frame is a Texture; the sound plays on the entity's og.AudioSource in step with it. |
| [`debug`](debug.md) | `og.debug.*` | dropped | Debug draw: lines, boxes, spheres, arrows, axes and labels in the world, each for a number of ticks, drawn over the finished frame (after every post effect, before the UI); and the debug views the command channel's `debug:` actions switch. |
| [`assert`](assert.md) | `og.assert.*` | dropped | Assertions: properties of the game checked as it runs, after the Antithesis SDK's (AssertKind: always, sometimes, reachable, unreachable, each). Each is identified by its name and the place it is called from, which the build records. Nothing an assertion does reaches the world, so a run with them hashes and replays as one without. Violations and coverage go through the probe (`assertions`) into `og run --json` and `og test`. |
| [`path`](path.md) | `og.path.*` | kept | Paths: a curve through or controlled by points, measured by arc length so a parameter t from 0 to 1 moves along it at an even speed. catmullRom passes through every point (tension 0.5), bezier chains cubic segments `p0 c0 c1 p1 c2 c3 p2 ...`, linear joins straight segments; a closed path joins its last point to its first and wraps t. |
| [`timeline`](timeline.md) | `og.timeline.*` | kept | Timelines: cutscenes and sequences as data, as an `.ogt` the agent reads and diffs (Unity's Timeline, Godot's AnimationPlayer): a `type timeline` file of keyed tracks (camera, transform, animation, audio, captions, events, shots, ...), cooked by `og cook` and loaded with og.load.timeline. |
| [`net`](net.md) | `og.net.*` | kept | Deterministic lockstep over a room (docs/design.md §2.10): every peer runs the whole world, and what crosses the room is each player's input, one per tick, and the world's hash. Turn it on with og.Lockstep and join a room (og.platform.roomJoin); once the room holds `players` peers the authority (the lowest peer number) starts, and tick t runs when every seated player's input for t is in (in rollback, on a prediction re-run when the input differs). |
| [`art`](art.md) | types and tokens | kept | A game's art contract: what every asset of its style holds, as seven resources a look sets beside the render ones (docs/art.md §2.1): ArtPalette, ArtPixels, ArtTexels, ArtShape, ArtLine, ArtMotion and ArtCamera. A style is the assets, not a filter on the frame. |
| [`motion`](motion.md) | `og.motion.*` | kept | Generated motion for humanoids: the engine's motion model moves a character between the game's goals, on the GPU. Give a humanoid og.Skeleton an og.MotionAgent, then queue goals (og.motion.walkTo, og.motion.jump, og.motion.pose, ...). |
| [`destruction`](destruction.md) | `og.destruction.*` | kept | Props that break (walls, crates, pillars, glass) and 2D ground that carves. A model cooked with a `fracture { }` block is cut by the cook into Voronoi chunks bonded where they touch; hits, og.destruction.damage and explode break an og.Destructible's bonds, each unanchored island falls as one body, and a stress solver (NVIDIA Blast's) breaks what can no longer carry its own weight. og.PixelTerrain is 2D ground of cells. |
| [`vfx`](vfx.md) | `og.vfx.*` | kept | Composed effects: one effect (a fireball's impact, a heal, a level-up) as a timeline of elements in an `.ogt` of `type vfx`: emitters, meshes, trails, beams, lights, decals, flashes, flipbooks, shakes and sounds. |
| [`sight`](sight.md) | `og.sight.*` | kept | Fog of war: which ground each team sees now and has seen before. An og.SightMap lays a grid over the og.Volume on its entity; every og.Sight is a team's eyes, and og.SightBlocker regions stop them. The map is world state, cast again as each tick starts: saved, restored and hashed with the world, the same on every host. The game asks it about a point (og.sight.visible, og.sight.explored), and the renderer draws the same cells over the frame. |

## Guides

Workflow, thresholds and pitfalls no signature states, written by hand beside the IDL (`crates/og-api/guides/`). `og api show <guide>` prints one; `og api find` returns their sections.

| Guide | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`animation`](guide-animation.md) | Motion in an Origin Engine game. Clips and animation graphs, og.motion's generated humanoid motion and why it is presentation only, tweens and timelines, and the timings that make actions read. |
| [`art-review`](guide-art-review.md) | Art judgment for an Origin Engine game. Choosing the style from the premise, requesting every asset through the art brief, the cook's conformance, and reviewing frames and models with measured thresholds. The engine measures; this guide says what is good enough. |
| [`assets`](guide-assets.md) | `og assets` searches the cooked asset inventory for reusable assets, unused outputs, dependencies, and duplicate content. `og cook` writes the inventory to `cooked/.assets.ogt`. The sidecar is not part of a web export. |
| [`audio`](guide-audio.md) | How a game makes sound: sources on entities, buses and their effects, spatial sound, music on a beat clock, mixer snapshots and reverb zones, the web's first-input unlock, and the voice budget. Sound is decided in the tick and rendered outside it: the engine's og.audio system turns og.AudioSource changes into a deterministic, time-stamped command stream that snapshots, restores and the world hash cover, and the host's mixer renders that stream to PCM, which never reaches the world. |
| [`camera`](guide-camera.md) | Which camera to drive the view with and how: an orbit or follow controller for a quick start, virtual cameras and the brain for a 3D game with shots, Follow2D with zones and rails for 2D, and shake, punch and kick for feel. Every camera here is visual only: it writes og.Camera, which the simulation never reads unless the game does, and a replay moves it the same on every host. |
| [`captures`](guide-captures.md) | How to look at a running game in as few tokens as possible: frames fitted for a model, crops at full resolution, numbered boxes that point back to source (Set-of-Mark), the key frames of a run with a timeline synced to ticks, and perceptual diff heat maps with the worst regions enlarged. The engine reports measurements and regions; what matters is the reader's call. |
| [`components`](guide-components.md) | Core elements and their reflected properties for scriptless Svelte documents. Unknown elements, properties, and values fail cooking. The `screens` guide describes contracts, bindings, styles, and content composition. |
| [`determinism`](guide-determinism.md) | The engine's rules a game must keep, determinism first, and where they bite: the world and systems, physics, destruction, and lockstep multiplayer over a room. Read before writing simulation code. |
| [`effect-packs`](guide-effect-packs.md) | Ready-made effects a game installs with `og vfx add <pack>`: converted Effekseer samples (`type vfx`, 3D) and pixel-art recipes (`type vfx2d`, 2D), each listed with its tags, keywords and effects. A bundled pack ships with the engine; a downloadable one comes with each release and `og vfx add` fetches it. Once installed, an effect spawns as `vfx/<pack>/<effect>` (`og api show vfx`; the `pixel-vfx` guide for `type vfx2d`); the pack format is docs/vfx-packs.md. |
| [`explore`](guide-explore.md) | How `og explore` searches a game's states for the bugs its playtests do not script, what it reports, how to act on a finding, and how to shape the search with GameDesc.explore. Read after the testing guide: explore checks the same invariants. |
| [`facing`](guide-facing.md) | Which way things face in the engine, how to turn them and read their directions, and how to turn a stick or WASD into a world direction that matches the screen. Read before writing movement, aiming or a camera rig; it is the one place the axes are stated. |
| [`input`](guide-input.md) | How a game reads the player: gameplay actions over keys, the mouse, touch and pads in action maps; mouse-look with the pointer lock; touch and virtual controls; gamepads with dead zones and rumble; the player's rebinding and the host-only session around it; and intents, injected input and replay. Everything the simulation reads is world state taken once per tick, so it replays and snapshots with the world. |
| [`loading`](guide-loading.md) | Loading what `og cook` made, and what a player or a generator makes at run time. This guide covers the import settings and asset files that each loader reads, what the cook does to them, streaming and residency, uncooked loads, and composed effects. |
| [`localization`](guide-localization.md) | How a game speaks the player's language: string tables per locale, ICU messages, locale selection and fallback, the font chain and right-to-left layout, and formatting numbers, money, dates and durations without reading a clock. Fonts per script and checking a screen in other locales are in `screens §6`; dialogue lines are in `yarn §2`. |
| [`looks`](guide-looks.md) | Rendering an Origin Engine game. The look as a preset the game extends, what belongs in the look and what in the scene, lighting and post order, 2D versus 3D, and what a frame costs. |
| [`models`](guide-models.md) | The `type model` asset: a prop or stylised character written as text from the engine's own geometry generators, cooked into the same model blob a glTF becomes. Use it when a model has to follow the look's shape language exactly, or when no catalogue or generated asset fits. |
| [`networking`](guide-networking.md) | How to choose and run a net mode: deterministic lockstep or rollback over a room, the input delay and prediction that hide latency, seats that drop and rejoin, desync detection and what to do about one, and rooms through og.platform. Every peer runs the whole world; what crosses the room is each player's input, one per tick, and the world's hash. The rules a simulation must keep to stay in step are in `determinism §1` and `determinism §3`. |
| [`physics`](guide-physics.md) | How to build a game's physical world on og.physics and og.destruction: which body and collider to pick, the units and the 2D or 3D profile, what queries and collision events see, how to tune the character controllers and vehicles, what the soft simulations (ropes, cloth, garments, soft bodies, fluids, ragdolls, buoyancy) cost, and how destruction is set up and budgeted. The determinism rules physics keeps are `determinism §2` and `determinism §4`; this guide does not repeat them. |
| [`pixel-vfx`](guide-pixel-vfx.md) | Pixel-art 2D effects (explosions, slashes, spells, portals, beams, auras, sparks, heals, level-ups, weather, loot) as `type vfx2d` files: a Pixel VFX Forge recipe, layered heat fields cut into hard colour bands, that the cook renders into a flipbook sheet with an `impact` event. |
| [`render`](guide-render.md) | The engine's render options and what each costs: tiers and quality presets, antialiasing and transparency, lights and shadows, global illumination and reflection, post effects, materials, atmosphere and water, interpolation, and secondary cameras. looks §3 covers how a scene is lit and looks §5 how to measure a frame; this guide says which engine option to turn on, when, and what it costs. |
| [`saves`](guide-saves.md) | How a game keeps the player's progress and talks to the platform: the save flow from world.snapshot through a save slot and back, whole saves and selections, what a save holds and what the session keeps, save versions and migrations, sizes and timings, and og.platform's calls (store, slots, leaderboards, purchases, identity, rooms), including a host that lacks a service. Read before writing a save system or a call to og.platform. |
| [`screens`](guide-screens.md) | Screens and HUDs for an Origin Engine game. The built-in screens and components and how to use, customise and review them, style packs and how to install and change them, documents versus code, the thresholds for text, contrast and touch, og ui check and preview, and languages with their fonts. |
| [`start`](guide-start.md) | Start here for any Origin Engine game: how a game begins from the empty skeleton and its create block, where the API is answered, the project's shape, and which guide covers what. |
| [`testing`](guide-testing.md) | The build, check and test loop of an Origin Engine game. Playtests as bun:test files, invariants first (og.assert, playtest invariants and require), frames only for looks, what an unchecked result means, the probe and dumps, and performance. |
| [`three-to-og`](guide-three-to-og.md) | For an author who knows three.js, or who has a three.js file to bring over. Origin Engine keeps three.js's vocabulary wherever it does not contradict the engine: `Vector3`, position, quaternion and scale, the material parameters, the geometry classes' parameters and defaults, glTF loading, layers. What it does not keep is the object model. A three.js program is a tree of mutable objects that a loop you write renders; an Origin Engine game is a world of entities with plain components, changed by systems on a fixed tick, and the engine draws every frame itself. Read the `start` and `determinism` guides first: this page only maps names. |
| [`ui-materials`](guide-ui-materials.md) | Per-element shader finishes for a game's UI: the foil, holo, burn and rarity presets of the `materials` resource pack, how to put one on a styled part or an element, how to tune it, and how to write a new one. |
| [`world`](guide-world.md) | How to build the ground a game is played on and what moves over it: terrain with its layers, scatter and grass; asset streaming groups and cells for large worlds; tilemaps for 2D; procedural generation; paths; navigation and crowds; and AI behaviours. Everything a tick reads here is deterministic and in snapshots; what only draws (grass, scatter, streamed tiles) never changes the world hash. |
| [`yarn`](guide-yarn.md) | Put dialogue in `assets/story/*.yarn`, then run `og cook`. Load the asset with `og.story.load(world, "story/smith.yarn")`. The cook compiles Yarn to engine-owned IR. The runtime, saves, quests, and UI views remain engine-owned. |

## Units

Field units the docs and Tune use.

| Unit | Means |
|---|---|
| `m` | metres |
| `s` | seconds of simulation time |
| `ms` | milliseconds |
| `rad` | radians: every rotation, heading, yaw, joint or steering limit, arc, uv rotation and cone; a cone is given as its half-angle |
| `deg` | degrees: a field of view (the full angle), a slope, the sky's angles (the sun's path, disc sizes, the aurora), camera roll, and the angles of post effects, styles and the art contract |
| `hz` | ticks or cycles per second |
| `ticks` | fixed simulation steps |
| `cssPx` | CSS pixels of the play surface, origin at the top left |
| `px` | pixels of an image, origin at its top left |
| `ratio` | a fraction between 0 and 1 |
| `bytes` | bytes |
| `kg` | kilograms |
| `newton` | newtons: the force that gives a kilogram one metre per second squared |
| `newtonSecond` | newton-seconds: an impulse, the momentum that changes a kilogram's velocity by one metre per second |
| `newtonMetre` | newton-metres: a torque, a newton pushing one metre from the axis it turns about |
| `mps` | metres per second |
| `mps2` | metres per second squared |
| `radps` | radians per second |
| `rpm` | revolutions per minute |
| `perSecond` | a rate per second: the fraction of a value that decays in one second |
| `kgPerM3` | kilograms per cubic metre (per square metre in the 2D profile) |
| `m3` | cubic metres |
| `pascal` | pascals: newtons per square metre, a stress |
| `newtonSecondPerM2` | newton-seconds per square metre: an impulse spread over an area |
| `db` | decibels |
| `evPerSecond` | exposure stops (EV) per second of simulation time |
| `bpm` | beats per minute |
